description: Introduce an AnalyticsReader port and a PostgresAnalyticsReader adapter, then make AnalyticsService depend on the port instead of Drizzle. This is Phase 4 of architecture epic #267 and closes issue #284. The refactor MUST be behavior-preserving: every Drizzle query moves VERBATIM (same SQL, same tables clickDaily/breakdownDaily/conversions/links, same READ_DB handle) from analytics.service.ts into the adapter. No query is 'improved'. Depends on FEAT-001 (green baseline). SCOPE: cover only what AnalyticsService.overview() reads today (totals-with-period-comparison, daily series, dimension breakdowns, top links, tag rollups, and the current/previous conversion totals overview needs). conversions.service.ts (report/record) is OUT OF SCOPE and documented as a follow-up candidate for the same port.
steps: Create apps/api/src/analytics/analytics.reader.ts. At the top, add a header block comment (mirroring the seam-documenting comment style in apps/redirect/src/resolver.ts and apps/redirect/src/click-sink.ts) that states: AnalyticsReader is the port for the analytics READ path; the Postgres adapter reads the rollup tables directly; this is the documented seam for a future ClickHouse or Timescale (columnar) adapter, NEITHER of which is built now; any adapter must return the same row shapes so downstream numbers cannot silently disagree.

In analytics.reader.ts, define `export interface AnalyticsReader` with methods shaped around exactly what overview() calls today. Suggested methods (name them clearly and drive their return types from the raw row shapes overview() consumes so the service maps them to @snapurl/contract types): totals(workspaceId, scopeLinkId, start): current totals { clicks, unique, scans, blocked }; previousTotals(workspaceId, scopeLinkId, previousStart, start): { clicks, unique, scans }; series(workspaceId, scopeLinkId, start): array of { date, clicks, unique, scans }; breakdown(workspaceId, dimension, start, linkId?): array of { label, value } (raw, UNLIMITED and UNMAPPED — the service applies the top-N slice and the city floor and country-name/flag mapping, exactly as today); tagBreakdown(workspaceId, start): array of { label, value }; topLinks(workspaceId, start): array of { label, value }; conversionTotals(workspaceId, scopeLinkId, start): number; previousConversionTotals(workspaceId, scopeLinkId, previousStart, start): number. IMPORTANT: preserve the current breakdown limit semantics — today overview() calls this.breakdown with limit=8 for country/device/browser/referrer and limit=0 (unlimited) for city (so applyCityFloor sees the whole tail). Keep that behavior: either the port returns unlimited rows and the service slices to 8 (cleanest), or the port takes the limit param verbatim. Pick one and keep the exact numbers so output is identical. Document the choice in a comment.

In analytics.reader.ts, define `export class PostgresAnalyticsReader implements AnalyticsReader` with `constructor(private readonly db: Database)` (the READ_DB replica handle). Move the Drizzle query bodies VERBATIM from analytics.service.ts into these methods: the current/previous clickDaily aggregate selects, the grouped-by-day series select, the breakdown() select over breakdownDaily, the tagBreakdown() join+unnest over clickDaily/links, the topLinks() join over clickDaily/links, and the two conversions count(*) selects. Keep the identical `scope` predicate construction (the `and(eq(clickDaily.workspaceId, ...), eq(clickDaily.linkId, ...))` vs `eq(clickDaily.workspaceId, ...)` branch) and the identical iso()-based date bounds. Move the Drizzle imports (and, breakdownDaily, clickDaily, conversions, desc, eq, gte, links, lt, sql, type Database) into this file. iso() is a pure helper the queries need — import it from analytics.service.ts (it is already exported) rather than duplicating it, so there is one source of truth for the date-key format.

Edit apps/api/src/analytics/analytics.service.ts: remove the `@snapurl/database` import entirely (no Drizzle query builders in this file anymore) and the `import { DB, READ_DB } from "../database/database.module.js"`. Import the ANALYTICS_READER token and the AnalyticsReader type. Change the constructor to inject only `@Inject(ANALYTICS_READER) private readonly reader: AnalyticsReader`. Rewrite overview() to call the reader methods instead of issuing Drizzle queries, keeping ALL store-agnostic logic in the service: windowFor()/period math, the scope decision (whether linkId is set), the Promise.all fan-out, applyCityFloor on the city breakdown, the top-8 slice for the other breakdowns (matching current behavior), COUNTRY_NAMES + FLAGS mapping on countries, fillSeries on the series, percentChange deltas, and assembling the final Analytics object with the identical field values. The service still exports all the pure helpers (applyCityFloor, CITY_MIN_CLICKS, OTHER_CITIES, iso, windowFor, percentChange, fillSeries).

Confirm the private breakdown/tagBreakdown/topLinks helpers are removed from AnalyticsService (their query bodies now live in the adapter). Any residual mapping the service still needs (top-8 slice, label mapping) lives inline in overview() or as a small pure helper, matching the current output exactly.

Add the DI token and wiring: in analytics.reader.ts (or analytics.module.ts, wherever mirrors the READ_DB pattern most closely) declare `export const ANALYTICS_READER = Symbol("ANALYTICS_READER")`. In apps/api/src/analytics/analytics.module.ts, add a provider `{ provide: ANALYTICS_READER, inject: [READ_DB], useFactory: (readDb: Database) => new PostgresAnalyticsReader(readDb) }` (import READ_DB from ../database/database.module.js and Database type from @snapurl/database). Keep AnalyticsService in providers and exported.

Update apps/api/src/analytics/analytics.service.test.ts: keep all existing pure-helper tests unchanged (25 assertions must still hold). Add a new describe block that constructs an AnalyticsService with a FAKE AnalyticsReader (a plain object implementing the interface with canned row data), calls overview(), and asserts the assembled Analytics response is correct — specifically that it proves the store-agnostic logic runs: the city floor folds sub-threshold cities into 'Other cities', country codes map to COUNTRY_NAMES + FLAGS, the top-8 slice is applied to non-city breakdowns, deltas use percentChange against the previous-window totals, series is zero-filled via fillSeries, and conversion totals/deltas come from the reader. This test must fail if the service stopped applying the floor/mapping/period logic, and directly evidences 'AnalyticsService depends on the port, not Drizzle'.

Run `corepack pnpm type-check`, `corepack pnpm build`, and `corepack pnpm test` and fix any issues. Then commit locally with a conventional-commit message referencing #284 (e.g. 'refactor(api): add AnalyticsReader port so the analytics store is swappable (#284)'). Do NOT push or open a PR.
acceptance_criteria: apps/api/src/analytics/analytics.reader.ts exists with `export interface AnalyticsReader` and `export class PostgresAnalyticsReader implements AnalyticsReader`, plus a header comment documenting the ClickHouse/Timescale seam (neither built).

All Drizzle queries that previously lived in analytics.service.ts (clickDaily/breakdownDaily/conversions/links selects) now live ONLY in PostgresAnalyticsReader, moved verbatim (same SQL, same predicates, same date bounds).
apps/api/src/analytics/analytics.service.ts imports NOTHING from @snapurl/database (verified by grep) and issues no query; it injects only the ANALYTICS_READER token.

AnalyticsService still owns and applies: applyCityFloor, COUNTRY_NAMES/FLAGS mapping, top-8 breakdown slice, windowFor period math, percentChange deltas, and fillSeries — producing an identical Analytics response to before.
analytics.module.ts binds ANALYTICS_READER -> PostgresAnalyticsReader via a useFactory off READ_DB, mirroring the database.module.ts token pattern.

The existing 25 analytics helper assertions still pass unchanged, AND a new test exercises AnalyticsService.overview() against a fake AnalyticsReader and asserts the floor/mapping/period/delta/fill logic.
`corepack pnpm type-check`, `corepack pnpm build`, and `corepack pnpm test` all pass; DB-gated integration tests SKIP locally as expected.
conversions.service.ts is unchanged; the boundary (report/record as a follow-up candidate for the port) is documented in a code comment in analytics.reader.ts.
verification: grep -n "clickDaily\|breakdownDaily\|conversions" apps/api/src/analytics/analytics.reader.ts confirms the queries live in the adapter only
findings: Introduced apps/api/src/analytics/analytics.reader.ts with `export interface AnalyticsReader`, `export class PostgresAnalyticsReader implements AnalyticsReader` (constructed off READ_DB), and `export const ANALYTICS_READER = Symbol("ANALYTICS_READER")`. Every Drizzle query moved VERBATIM from analytics.service.ts into the adapter (totals/previousTotals/series/breakdown/tagBreakdown/topLinks/conversionTotals/previousConversionTotals over clickDaily/breakdownDaily/conversions/links); same SQL, same scope-predicate branch, same iso()-based date bounds. iso() is imported from analytics.service.ts (single source of truth). Design choice: breakdown() returns UNLIMITED value-descending rows; the service applies the top-8 slice (via a small pure topN helper) to country/device/browser/referrer and passes the whole city tail to applyCityFloor, preserving the exact prior behavior. analytics.service.ts now imports NOTHING from @snapurl/database (grep confirms) and injects only @Inject(ANALYTICS_READER); it retains all store-agnostic logic (applyCityFloor, COUNTRY_NAMES/FLAGS mapping, top-8 slice, windowFor, percentChange, fillSeries) and the exported pure helpers. analytics.module.ts binds ANALYTICS_READER -> PostgresAnalyticsReader via useFactory off READ_DB. Seam for a ClickHouse/Timescale columnar adapter is documented in the reader header (neither built); conversions.service.ts left unchanged and noted as a follow-up candidate in a bottom-of-file comment. Tests: existing 25 pure-helper assertions unchanged; added a 6-assertion describe block that builds AnalyticsService with a FAKE AnalyticsReader and asserts overview() applies the floor/country-mapping/top-8/period-delta/fill/conversion logic (analytics.service.test.ts now 31 tests). Verification: full `corepack pnpm type-check`, `corepack pnpm build` (with NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://api.example.com/api/v1), and `corepack pnpm test` all pass; DB-gated integration tests skip locally as expected (Postgres 18 cannot start in sandbox).
